newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk police arrest three in Islamist charity probe.
newsitem.headline: Turk police arrest three in Islamist charity probe.

text.p: Turkish police arrested three officials of a charitable foundation linked to the Islam-based Welfare Party as part of a legal investigation, Anatolian news agency said on Monday.
The agency said the three National Youth Foundation (MGV) officials had been arrested in Nevsehir province following searches of the organisation's premises.
Police seized videotapes featuring controversial Islamist politicians and illegal religious books at the offices.
Prosecutors said they had decided to pursue a legal investigation into the MGV after searching foundation premises nationwide.

"We opened the investigation after searching the premises of the National Youth Foundation...The reason for this is that the MGV had become a focus of activities against the secular nature of the state," Ankara prosecutor Nuh Mete Yuksel told Reuters.
Yuksel said that during the searches of MGV premises prosecutors found evidence implicating the foundation in political activities. Under Turkish law, charitable foundations must be non-political.
The investigation is the first step which could lead to prosecution and closure of the MGV -- commonly regarded as the youth wing of Welfare.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, was forced to resign in June after months of pressure by the secularist establishment led by the powerful military.
His party faces a separate threat of closure on charges it sought to undermine Turkey's official secular order.
